rich_narrative.summary: The Against Malaria Foundation (AMF) is a global health organization focused on the <cite id="1">funding and provision of long-lasting insecticidal nets</cite> (LLINs) to protect populations at risk of malaria. In FY2025, the organization reported <cite id="2">total revenue of $62,286,888</cite> to support its distribution and monitoring efforts. AMF operates with a highly specialized model, primarily serving regions in <cite id="3">Africa, Asia, and South America</cite> where malaria remains a leading cause of death. The organization is characterized by an extreme focus on financial efficiency, reporting a <cite id="4">100.0% program expense ratio in FY2025</cite>. This means all public donations are directed toward program costs, while private donors cover administrative overhead. Despite this efficiency, the organization faces limitations in its <cite id="5">governance structure</cite> and its alignment with specific faith-based donor requirements. While it holds a <cite id="6">91/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, its internal assessment is lower due to minimal board oversight and a lack of cultural tailoring for Muslim communities. The charity's work is strictly limited to <cite id="7">capacity building and net distribution</cite>, rather than broader medical or humanitarian interventions.
